verdict: v3 is clearly and obviously better looking than v2 almost everywhere I looked, on both backends and every preset, and I found no blocker. Kit has real fur, eyes and outfit; the city has wood siding, interior-mapped shop windows and SSR puddles; the vehicles have proper bodies, wheels and lamps; Act 1 has grass blades, PBR path and sand, and a lit cloud sky. The phone Moyen + Super Résolution view (844x390, dpr 3, touch UI) reads well and its HUD is legible. WebGPU and WebGL 2 match: G-a1start vs h-a1start mean |diff| 1.03, 0.13% of pixels > 30. Every number in my runs is within the SPEC3 budgets. Highest scene-pass counts: Ultra 194 calls / 1.83 M tris, Élevé 196 / 1.39 M, Moyen+SR 151 / 0.78 M (a2street-medium-sr: 781,559 tris, only 2% under the 800 k Moyen limit), Économie 146 / 0.68 M. All of my browser runs and probes logged 0 console errors. Four problems are clearly visible and, as far as I can tell, not covered by the integrator's remaining_issues: (1) In the loops, velocity motion blur turns Kit into a translucent ghost on Ultra, Élevé and Moyen, on both backends and on the phone. v2 showed him crisp. This happens in every frame of a sequence drawn each tick at 60 Hz, so it is not an artefact of the harness. (2) During the bumper flight, the fog-bank billboards cut the water with a hard straight line. (3) The Act 1 checker cliffs show no rock texture or normal detail at play distance: their high-frequency detail is at film-grain level, the same as clear sky. (4) On Ultra, the SSGI ambient occlusion makes the grass blades flicker on a perfectly still frame, about 3x more than on Élevé. The minor issues are: ragged, salmon-coloured tail lamps on the van and the delivery van; rings paler and less gold than v2; cable-car rails that still read as saturated blue strips in shade; flat box totems. I checked and dropped three candidates: the goal sign showing its back (it is mid-spin; at rest it shows the face), the translucent legs at top speed (the 'peel' wheel, already in v2), and foliage ghosting in free-camera shots (a harness clock artefact). I also looked at shadows, SSR, the DOF in cinematics and colour space and found nothing wrong to report. I did not do a dedicated hunt for CSM cascade seams or LOD popping in motion. Method: my own harness dev/review-visual/rv.js, which is the integrator's shoot.js plus frame sequences. `@still` sequences freeze the clock and only re-render, so the TAA jitter is the only thing that changes between frames; `@tick` sequences draw every tick. Measurements come from dev/review-visual/py/*.py (temporal std, high-pass detail, hue-band saturation, row profiles), crops are in dev/review-visual/shots/c-*.png, and v2 comparisons use the v2 shots in the scratchpad.

findings.title: Motion blur turns Kit into a translucent ghost through the loops (Ultra, Élevé, Moyen; WebGL 2, WebGPU and phone)
findings.file: src/15-post.js (velocity motion blur: U.mb / U.mbVel, the pass at ~line 466; PRESETS mb 12/8/6)
findings.evidence: View a1loopkit in dev/review-visual/rv.js. Kit is at about (471,292); speed 30.6 m/s, post speed 0.43. Crop dev/review-visual/shots/c-loopkit-high-nomb-low-ultra.png, panels from left to right: Élevé, Élevé with motion blur off (pseudo-view mb=0), Économie, Ultra. With motion blur off and on Économie Kit is solid; on Élevé and Ultra he is a pale cyan/orange ghost with the track showing through. The same holds on Moyen (dev/review-visual/shots/c-loopkit-medium-vs-nomb.png), on WebGPU (dev/review-visual/shots/c-loopkit-gpu-vs-gl.png), on the phone (dev/review-visual/shots/M-a1loop.png, Kit near (1050,500) in the 2532x1170 shot) and in the integrator's shots/v3-a1loop.png. Sequence drawn every tick at 60 Hz (a1loopkit@tick6): dev/review-visual/shots/c-loopkit-seq.png, Kit is a ghost in every frame. Numbers vs motion blur off, mean |diff| in Kit's box 440,265-520,330 against a cliff box: Élevé 18.4 vs 6.2, Ultra 20.0 vs 7.0, Moyen 11.5 vs 2.8. Value of Kit's orange top 25% (py/hue.py, box 430,260,530,330, hue 10-35): 0.43 with motion blur off, 0.44 Économie, 0.30 Élevé, 0.24 Ultra, 0.27 Moyen. v2 05-loop.png shows Kit opaque.
findings.fix_hint: The loop camera is fixed, so Kit crosses the screen fast and gets a full 1/60 s (360°) shutter plus the radial streak term. Keep the player sharp: tag Kit in the velocity MRT (zero his velocity, or use a mask), or clamp the blur length per pixel. Also consider a 180° shutter (halve U.mbVel) and capping the blur length in pixels.

findings.title: Bumper flight: the fog-bank billboards cut the bay water with a hard straight horizontal line (plus a faint vertical billboard edge)
findings.evidence: Crop dev/review-visual/shots/c-flight-fogedge.png: on the left, dev/review-visual/shots/h-kitflight.png at y≈546; on the right, dev/review-visual/shots/h-a2flight.png at y≈503. A straight hazy band ends on a hard line across the water. Row-mean luma (x 40-1200) in h-kitflight drops 144.2 -> 133.2 -> 119.1 -> 111.8 over rows 545-548, a 32-level step within 3 rows on otherwise smooth water. In h-a2flight it drops 190 -> 173 at y=503. The edge reproduces on WebGPU (dev/review-visual/shots/G-kitflight.png, y=540, -11.1 per row) and in the integrator's shots/v3-kitflight.png (y=545, 3-row drop 28.3). In fogMesh, opacity uses softFade(viewDepth(c0), 12): with a 12 m fade range against 70-160 m billboards over water seen at a grazing angle, the soft-particle fade collapses to 1-3 pixel rows. dev/review-visual/fogtex.js reproduces fogTexture(): the alpha on the canvas border is 0.146 in the right column and 0.026 in the left, so blobs are clipped and leave a vertical edge (visible at x≈415 in the left half of the crop). The integrator's remaining_issues mention only haze, not this edge.
findings.fix_hint: Scale the soft-fade range with the billboard size (for example aOff.w * 0.3-0.5), or fade on the depth difference divided by its screen derivative. Keep the fog blobs inside the canvas (centre within [r, 128-r]) or multiply alpha by an edge window such as smoothstep on uv.x and uv.y.

findings.title: Act 1 checker cliffs show no rock texture or normal detail at play distance (flat colour, same as v2)
findings.file: src/20-world.js groundMaterial() checker branch (gChk / chkBump, ~line 397-415): w-terrain and w-decor meshes
findings.evidence: Crop dev/review-visual/shots/c-cliff-flat.png (left: h-a1lakeside 40,380-340,700; right: h-a1cliffclose 300,500-560,720): flat orange and brown planes with bevel lines and no strata, cracks or bump. py/detail.py (std of luma minus a 7x7 box blur): h-a1water.png cliff 100,100,800,600 = 1.96, h-a1cliffclose.png 330,560,520,700 = 1.91, h-a1bridge.png 1080,200,1240,380 = 1.98. Clear sky in the same frame (h-a1water 1100,40,1250,200) = 1.89, so the cliffs carry only film grain. For comparison, the dirt path (h-a1start 700,500,1000,650) = 9.61 and the pier boards (h-a2pier) = 12.8. The generated texture has strong strata and cracks (dev/review-visual/shots/tex-rock_albedo.png; luma std/mean 0.111). It is loaded (K.tex 28/28, rock_* in the act1 group), and the raycast probe dev/review-visual/probe-cliff.js (dev/review-visual/logC.txt) shows that w-terrain and w-decor draw these faces. SPEC3 §5 asks for 'real rock/soil materials with normal detail'. This is not the known 'triangular patches' issue.
findings.fix_hint: Debug-output rA and chkBump on a cliff face. Likely suspects: the texture weight (mix 0.7 times meanInv), and a 1.3 m repeat (gq*1.9) that minifies the strata and cracks into a low mip at 3-15 m. Use a larger macro scale for the strata (for example 1 repeat per 2.5 m square or less), add a second detail octave, and give the rock normal more strength than nXY(rN, 0.6).

findings.title: Ultra: SSGI ambient occlusion makes the grass blades flicker on a still frame (about 3x Élevé)
findings.file: src/15-post.js SSGI branch (~line 288-300: sliceCount 2, stepCount 8, AO multiplied into lit)
findings.evidence: Still sequences have the clock, world and camera frozen, so only the TAA jitter advances (verified with dev/review-visual/probe-freeze.js: world, post and node time are constant). Grass box 300,460,1248,720 in a1grass@still, py/tstab.py, % of pixels with temporal std > 8 (and % with |frame diff| > 20, f05->f06): Ultra 25.2% (12.4%), Ultra with gi=0 22.3% (11.6%), Ultra with gi=0 and ao=0 8.2% (6.6%), Élevé 6.2% (4.1%), Moyen+SR 3.9% (2.6%), Moyen 2.9% (1.5%). Turning off the SSGI AO term (uniform ao=0) removes most of the flicker; GI does not. Heat map dev/review-visual/shots/P-a1grass-ultra-sdmap.png: whole blades and the near rings light up. Compare dev/review-visual/shots/h-a1grass-sdmap.png (Élevé, edges only) and the 3-frame crop dev/review-visual/shots/c-grass-ultra-frames.png. Frames: dev/review-visual/shots/P-a1grass-ultra-f*.png and X-a1grass-ultra-gi0*-f*.png.
findings.fix_hint: Thin alpha-tested blades are undersampled with 2 slices x 8 steps. Options: take AO on Ultra from GTAO (or more SSGI slices and steps) and keep SSGI for GI only; exclude grass blades and rings from SSGI AO (mask or thickness); or clamp the AO in the TRAA neighbourhood before it multiplies the lit colour.

findings.title: Van and delivery-van tail lamps render as ragged salmon slivers (the curved body pokes through the lamp patch)
findings.file: src/26-vehicles.js van rear lamps: patch(vb, S, true, 1, 3, ..., -2.2], () => [0, 0, -1], 0.006, VK.TAIL, ...) (~line 684)
findings.evidence: Views vanrear and dvanrear in dev/review-visual/rv.js: dev/review-visual/shots/X-vanrear.png, dev/review-visual/shots/X-dvanrear.png, zoomed crop dev/review-visual/shots/c-vanrear-lamps.png. Each lamp is a torn, irregular shape with body paint showing through. Lamp pixels average rgb (252,195,160), a clipped salmon, while the sedan and taxi tail lamps in dev/review-visual/shots/h-vehcars.png are (248,102,76). It is also visible at play distance: dev/review-visual/shots/c-van-lamps.png (P-a2street-low.png at x≈1190-1250, y≈520-670; h-vehcars.png at x≈1210-1250, y≈540-600).
findings.fix_hint: A 1 x 3 patch spans the strongly curved rear corner, so its flat quads cut into the body. Subdivide across (nu >= 4), raise the offset (about 0.015-0.02) or add a polygon offset. Also check the tail emissive on this lamp (it reads salmon, not red).

findings.title: Gold rings look pale and brassy, much less saturated than v2
findings.file: src/40-entities.js ringMaterial() (GOLD (1,0.5,0.07) full metal + emissive bands (1.0,0.78,0.3))
findings.evidence: py/hue.py, hue 36-62, top-25% most saturated pixels. v3 in 7 views across both acts: sat 0.61-0.66, rgb about (198,160,72). Boxes: h-a1start 372,268,414,304; 834,276,872,320; h-a1valley 460,185,580,335; h-a1cliffs 565,565,715,680; h-a1bridge 595,335,690,440; h-a1lake 615,270,870,530; h-a2traffic 90,20,360,250. v2 03-start.png: sat 0.98-1.00, rgb (211,156,5). Crops: dev/review-visual/shots/c-rings-v2-v3.png (v2 left, v3 right) and dev/review-visual/shots/c-rings-v3-close.png.
findings.fix_hint: The blue-sky reflection times gold plus the pale yellow band emissive desaturates the rings. Use a deeper gold for the emissive bands (for example 1.0, 0.62, 0.12), tint the reflection, or slightly lower the band strength.

findings.title: Cable-car rails still read as saturated blue painted strips in shade (and clip with bloom into the sun)
findings.file: src/25-city.js rail surface kind (rail roughness / colour in cityMaterial)
findings.evidence: Crops dev/review-visual/shots/c-a2traffic-rails.png and dev/review-visual/shots/c-a2street-rails.png. Rail top 25% in h-a2traffic.png box 615,520,650,720: rgb (40,62,120), sat 0.66, against the asphalt around it at (29,34,70). In h-a2street.png 60,540,380,700 the rails are (24,35,76), sat 0.67. Into the low sun, the waterfront rails peak at luma 251-254 in rows 420-540 (x 823-910), against an asphalt median of 147-189 in the same rows, and they bloom (dev/review-visual/shots/c-waterfront-rails.png, from h-a2waterfront.png). The integrator lists this as fixed ('no longer read as neon-blue lines'); they are less neon but still read as blue strips.
findings.fix_hint: Shaded steel should take the warm and pink ambient: lower the environment/specular contribution of the rail kind, raise roughness further in the groove, or darken its albedo. A specular clamp on rails would tame the sun glints.

findings.title: Act 1 totem props are untextured flat boxes with painted faces at close range
findings.evidence: Crop dev/review-visual/shots/c-totems.png (h-a1start.png 1170,160-1262,440 and 16,160-110,440; h-kit34.png 16,0-200,470): flat yellow and blue boxes with square eyes, next to fully textured rocks, grass and Kit.
findings.fix_hint: Use the wood material (world/wood_*) with bevels for the totems, or the entities' painted-metal look.
